author_fan_clumps_field.py.status: new; the first R03 or R04 order writes it

spec.envelope: the sheet fan outline per view from sheet.json (front, back, left) plus a depth plan of the fan's front and rear surfaces on a (u, y) grid in fit units; the outline that already passes is the target
spec.strip: the field zone to clear before growing: everything of the old fan in front of (part front) or behind (part rear) the fan mid-surface, outside a protected skull mask (the R01 skull ellipsoids plus .006) and outside the face window of graft_face_field.py; the cleared zone is replaced by an inner core inset .010 to .015 from the envelope so no clump gap shows through
spec.roots: root band polylines: the ear-root crease (R01 spec masses 3 and 4), the cup rim (R03), and for the rear the crown line and rear root band
spec.clumps: list of {id, root (x, y, df), path (3 to 5 control points, or direction, length, curl and droop), section {widthRoot, widthMid, thickMid, roundness 1.0 to 1.8}, twistDeg, taperExp, tipRadius, layer, material}
spec.cup: {polygon, floor depth table, opening normal (yaw out from forward, pitch), rim radius}; carved after the coat clumps, before the tuft
spec.tuft: pale clumps inside the cup, same fields as clumps, material 'Pale inner-ear coat'
spec.blend: smooth-union radii per layer and a light per-clump field blur before fusing (LESSONS: short tapered cones leave ribs)

author_fan_clumps_field.py.outputs: head.blend, shape.glb, fan-clumps.json (per clump length, section and tip stats, envelope missing and extra area per view, cup and tuft coverage, skinTopZ, skinAfter components and nonManifoldEdges), source-snapshot/
author_fan_clumps_field.py.invariants: one closed component; skinTopZ no higher than the baseline's (LESSONS: cap the figure height); no geometry change outside the fan zone (recipe.py contain)
author_fan_clumps_field.py.recipe: two steps after H33: the R04 rear step first, then the R03 front step, so the front unions last. Once both pass, H27, H28, H31, H32 and H33 build geometry that is stripped again and can be dropped in a later recipe cleanup, with H30 rebased on H26.

R01.name: Head silhouette
R01.method: Skull and jaw authored as smooth-union ellipsoids (skulls[] plus the chin and cut tables) in shape_head_silhouette_field.py at step H25, raising the crown dome between the ear roots from its own ellipsoid rather than the crown_lift surface warp.
R01.why: Closes gap rank 8 (flat forehead band and square jaw; R01.3 and R01.5 partial): crown height and jaw section are structure, and a skull ellipsoid sets them from parameters where round 2's crown_lift only warped the existing roof by a hair. The back-view dome sunk behind seams (rank 1, R01.4) is left to the fan rebuild, which strips the shell around the skull.
R01.failureLooks: Crown nubs or a bald bulb poking above the fan top (figure height grows; check skinTopZ); a window-edge crease ring around the lifted dome; a chin knob or a pinched stem under a narrowed jaw; the fan top edge pulled down beside the crown (the sunk roof).
R01.stallNext: Author the skull and head base as one lofted section stack from the R01 head base table and sheet.json head stations (a new head-base generator), morphed into the native field below the fan root band.

R02.name: Face
R02.method: Subdivision-surface face patch after the assembly: a new author_face_subd_patch.py builds the face window as an authored quad cage from the spec tables (concentric eye loops for socket, rim, lid fold and an opened lateral wall; a nose wedge with a creased triangular pad face; muzzle lobes; each cheek tuft extruded from the cage as a shingled flap with a creased point), conforms the cage's free vertices to the F-bulk donor surface by ray heightfield, Catmull-Clark subdivides it three levels and swaps it into the assembled skin through finish_face_assembled.py's window replacement and zipper; the lid band and nose pad are material faces of the patch between set loops, and the eye globe and iris lens stay retained objects.
R02.steps: new: author_face_subd_patch.py as A-face-subd, a post-assembly step replacing A-face (same place in RECIPE.md Post-assembly steps, after the .0028 world remesh, before the packet render and posing); F-bulk kept as the donor surface; H29 and H30 kept. It imports finish_face_assembled.py's window, zipper, globe and iris functions instead of copying them. The first order writes the tool and builds a control that matches the baseline face (baseline eye size, round 10 pad outline, two broad locks) and must reach 8.3 before any variant is judged, then a build at the R02.md tables.
R02.interface: blender art/species-construction/author_face_subd_patch.py -- --asm {asm} --out {out} --donor <F-bulk head.blend> --spec <r02-subd.json> (head-local coordinates through assembly.json headTransform, as in finish_face_assembled.py). Spec: window (as A-face), cage {gridX, gridZ, levels 3}, eye {center, semi, rings: list of {offset from the aperture, depth, crease} for socket floor, rim, fold edge and brow, lateralOpenDeg, bandPercent table mapped to the faces between the rim loop and a band loop, globe and iris keys as A-face}, nose {tip, topEdge, apex, cornerRadius, front radius, side angle, padCrease, wrapUnder}, muzzle {lobe center, radius, philtrumDepth}, tufts [{root, tip, length, widthRoot, widthMid, thickMid, liftThird, tipCrease, shingleUnder}], border {feather rings}. Outputs akinza.glb and akinza.blend in the assembly layout (one closed skin plus retained globe and iris objects), cage.blend and cage.png (front and profile wireframe over the render, for the builder and critic), face-parts.json with A-face's metrics plus tuft outline standoff and pad outline points, source-snapshot/. Invariants: skin one closed component (I08), figure height unchanged (I09), no skin change outside the window, zero non-manifold edges.
R02.why: The post-assembly step did what it was built for: round 27's tool check and three variants built clean with no seam or remesh loss, so precision is no longer the limit. What it exposed is that the level-set primitives are hard-edged once nothing blurs them: the tool record says the starter tufts read as creased facets and the pad top as a ledge, the lens locks sharpened the profile slab edge that cost round 27, and the triangular pad outline cut into the philtrum groove and hung a drip-shaped stem below the nose (readers 2 of 3 worse). The baseline's soft face was partly the coarse remesh smoothing those primitives. A subdivided quad cage is soft by construction and sets each feature by where its loops sit and which edges are creased, so rounded lens locks with true points (R02.5, gap rank 14), a seated triangular pad with no stem (R02.3), the upper-heavy band as faces between loops (R02.2, R02.6) and an opened lateral eye wall for the profile oval (gap ranks 3 and 9) all become cage geometry instead of field blends.
R02.failureLooks: A rubbery, inflated face where subdivision rounds everything (pad and tuft tips with no point, lids with no edge); visible grid lines or pinching at poles where eye and tuft loops meet the grid; a cage that floats off the donor surface or self-intersects at the extruded tufts; a crease or shading step at the window border; band faces that alias into a stepped band at low cage density; brow and nose no longer in front of the eye (R02.6); locks as sausages or fins; extra components or non-manifold edges at the zipper.
R02.stallNext: Hand-authored face patch: one reference quad cage modeled from r01 and R02.png (eye, nose, muzzle and tuft loops), stored as an asset and only fitted to the head by the window conform, so the face is a sculpted part rather than a generated one; if that also stalls, the region holds at 8.3 for the surface phase.
R02.respecReason: Carried from rounds 21 and 25 and never applied: specs/R02.md still describes the eye as a skin rim over the globe all round with a closed lateral wall, the eye front at least .010 behind the brow-to-nose line, no profile visibility target and a .52 convergent iris, the structure that makes the profile wedge; a cage built from it would build the wedge again. The rewrite states the opened lateral wall and the profile target (closed oval about .30 of head height, width at mid height at least half its height, iris at least the front third, looking forward), a front iris of .5 to .6 of the eye width offset toward the gaze, the lid band as faces between the rim loop and a band loop with the bandPercent table, and the pad as a creased face of the nose wedge ending above the philtrum root. Tuft table, nose wedge outline, muzzle and lower face rows stay.

review.trigger: loop plateau (last rounds gained under .15 together), R02 ranked highest
review.stall: The A-face step removed the remesh loss but no candidate beat the baseline: round 27, the only round on it, lost on a drip-shaped stem under the nose and a hard slab edge in profile, and the tool record already said the starter tufts read as creased facets and the pad top as a ledge. At the fine voxel the level-set primitives (lens locks unioned by a blend, an outline-cut pad recess) keep the hard construction edges the coarse remesh used to soften, so more A-face parameters trade softness against shape inside the same primitives, as rounds 22 to 27 did with blends from .015 to .045.

R03.name: Ear fan front
R03.method: Coat locks finished after the assembly remesh, cup and tuft kept: a new post-assembly step finish_fan_assembled.py (kind post) keeps the baseline H33 fan (its cup, pale tuft, outline and drape) and, only inside a coat window that excludes each cup polygon plus a .006 margin, strips the remeshed front coat to a backing and cuts in fan_lock_sweeps' coat locks (about ten primaries per side, cup and tuft builders off) through a fine level set (.0008 head-local) zipped into the .0028 world skin, so undercuts, tip standoff and true points are never remeshed; the same pass reseals the crinkled tuft and cup-wall seams at the fine voxel without moving the tuft.
R03.steps: new: A-fan, a post-assembly step after the assembly (and after A-face when the recipe has it), running finish_fan_assembled.py; H33 stays the fan source and H36 (any author_fan_lock_sweeps version) is not in the recipe. The first order writes the script from finish_face_assembled.py (head transform, window replacement, fine level set, zipper) plus fan_lock_sweeps.build_wing with cup and tuft disabled, and runs two controls: an empty lock set (must reproduce the baseline render within the window seam check) and the round 16 primaries from r03_clumps.json.
R03.interface: blender art/species-construction/finish_fan_assembled.py -- --asm <assembly dir> --out <new assembly dir> --table specs/r03_clumps.json --envelope specs/r03_envelope.npz --spec specs/r03_fan_assembled.json [--voxel .0008]. Coordinates as finish_face_assembled.py (head-local = (world - offset)/scale from assembly.json headTransform; fit units = head-local/3.721). Spec: window {cupMargin (default .006 figure heights), cupPolygons (from the baseline pale faces, measured, not authored), uMin, yMax, seamBlend}; strip {maxDepth, depthRamp}; backing {depthBehindDeepest, minThickness}; layers [{ids, standoff, undercut, lengthScale}]; section {p, spine, twistDeg, rollDeg, widthScale, thickScale}; tips {minHalfWidth at least 2 x the fine voxel, length, upFlare per wing-end lock}; union {rootBand, rootBlend}; reseal {cupWallBand, voxel, smooth}; clumps (per-lock edits); skip. Outputs akinza.blend and akinza.glb in the assembly layout, fan-assembled.json (per lock tip standoff and tip radius measured on the final mesh, envelope missing and extra per view, crown-to-tip drop per side, pale area front and side, cup window changed vertices (must be 0 outside the reseal band), skin components, nonManifoldEdges, darkHoles), source-snapshot/. Invariants: skin one closed component (I08), figure height unchanged (I09), no skin change outside the coat window and the reseal band.
R03.why: It keeps what readers preferred in all three reverted rounds (the baseline cup and pale tuft, R03.5 partial and the tuft half of R03.7) and puts the lock sweeps where their premise holds: after the remesh, so the undercut and points that R03.4, R03.3's up-flared tips and the edge half of R03.7 need survive to the render, and the crinkled tuft seams (status issue 2) are resealed at a fine voxel instead of widened blends.
R03.failureLooks: A visible window seam or step where the fine coat meets the .0028 remeshed skin or the kept cup rim; the cup margin eaten so the rim or tuft moves; pine cone shingles (standoff too small, sections too flat); dark slits where the backing shows; tips leaving the envelope or wing tops falling so R03.1, R03.2 or the figure height moves; the reseal smoothing the tuft points away; the step drifting from the head transform; posed renders built from the pre-step mesh; extra skin components.
R03.stallNext: Retained lock shells: each coat lock a separate closed shell object kept after the assembly like the eye and iris objects, rooted into the skin by overlap with no union, so undercut and point are exact by construction and only placement is tuned.
R03.respecReason: specs/R03.md still describes the coat clump volume and a rebuilt cup (35 degree floor, carve, T1 to T5 tuft on the floor, overlap order with the core). Under this method the cup and tuft are the baseline's and only resealed, so the spec must name them as kept (with the measured baseline polygons as the coat window's exclusion and the tuft seam rule), keep the clump table P rows, envelope and tip targets, and add the coat window, backing, standoff and undercut, up-flared wing-end tips and the post-assembly measurement points.

review.trigger: loop plateau (last rounds gained under .15 together), R03 ranked highest; rounds 21, 23, 24 reverted
review.stall: Rounds 21, 23 and 24 all reverted, and every reader reason names the inner ear first: the baseline's pale cupped tufted bowls beat the rebuilt cup and tuft each time (flat slabs and ribbed slats in 21, long flat leaf blades edged by dark seam gaps and a torn rim in 23, 5.7 to 5 in 24). Every sweep variant rebuilt the cup and tuft together with the coat, so whatever the coat locks gained was spent on the part the baseline already does best; and the sweep step runs at H36, before the assembly voxel-remeshes the fused skin at .0028 world (.0056 head-local, about .0015 figure heights), where the tool's tips (half width .0035) are about two voxels and its undercuts and slits less than that, so the gaps between solids partly fill and tear into the dark slits and ragged rim the readers named. That is the regime the round 25 R02 review found; more H36 levers would retune inside it.

Spec: {strip (as now), backing {depthBehindDeepest}, layers [{ids, standoff, undercut}], section {p, spine, twistDeg default}, tips {minHalfWidth >= 2 x output voxel}, union {rootBand, voxel, blend}, cup {rim, floor, yawDeg, pitchDeg, fillet}, tuft {ids, standoff, pale}}. Outputs head.blend, shape.glb, fan-sweeps.json (per lock tip standoff achieved, tip radius, envelope missing and extra per view, cup opening normal and pale area front and side, skinTopZ, components, nonManifoldEdges), source-snapshot/. Invariants: one closed component, skinTopZ not above the baseline, no change outside the fan zone (recipe.py contain).
previous.why: Closes gap-audit-2278 ranks 1 and 2 and the failing R03.3, R03.4, R03.5 and R03.7, which round 21 showed the clump volume cannot reach: its core fills the envelope and its grooves and tips sit at one to three voxels, so the front reads as a smooth crumpled shell whatever the clump levers. Separate solids with tip standoff give each lock a shadowed undercut and a true point at mesh resolution, the cup becomes a shaped bowl instead of a square carve, and the tuft becomes pointed clumps instead of slabs; the clump table, envelope and outline that already pass (R03.1 1.021, R03.2 .035) carry over.
previous.failureLooks: Pine cone or shingled scales (even rows of flat leaves, standoff too small or sections too flat, as rounds 12 to 16); sausages or spaghetti (even round tubes, no spine, blunt ends); dark holes where the backing shows between locks; a visible root seam or step where the fine union meets the coarse head; thin whisker tips or ball ends; tips leaving the envelope so figure height or R03.1 moves; the cup still reading as a square window or facing only forward; more than one component or non-manifold edges from a boolean.
previous.stallNext: Groomed hair curves to clumps: Blender hair curves grown from the root bands, clumped into 8 to 10 primaries per side with the hair clump and frizz-free settings, converted with curve-to-mesh on a thick tapered profile and joined as above, so the lock layout comes from a groom instead of a table.
previous.respecReason: The spec's strip-and-core section (core inset .006 behind the envelope, grooves .004 to .008 deep, union radii per layer) and its cup carve describe the field construction that flattened the front. The new method needs per-lock layer, tip standoff and undercut over the lock beneath, section spine and twist, a backing depth instead of a core, the root-band union, and the cup as a bowl surface (rim curve, floor table, opening yaw and pitch, rim fillet). The clump table rows (roots, tips, lengths, widths, thicknesses, curl) and the envelope stay.
previous.review: Round 21 (parked: 3 rounds without a net gain of 1). The clump tool ran as specified and did not change the read: assembled-2412 and the refine candidates 2462 to 2464 all scored 'same' on R03 and R04, and m04 shows the front as a smooth shell with a crumpled, spiky rim, a square-walled cup window and a tuft of stacked horizontal slabs (venetian blind in the side view). The cause is in the field, not the levers: the core was run at core_inset 0, so it fills the whole envelope, and the clumps add only .004 to .008 of relief over it on a .0025 voxel grid with a 2-voxel blur and .004 to .005 unions, so every groove is one to three voxels deep and melts, while the tip floors (.002, tuft .0012) are below one voxel and break into thorns. The nine ideas and the width sweep moved levers inside that same regime, so they could not differ (v01 and v02 measured identically). Envelope plus relief, the planned stall method, is the same regime by construction: a displaced envelope has no undercut, and the missing undercut is what keeps the locks from reading.

previous.method: Coat clump volume: guide curves grown from the ear-root crease and cup rim into the sheet's fan envelope, each swept as a thick tapering clump of rounded section, converted to OpenVDB level sets and smooth-unioned over a small inset core, with the ear cup carved to open forward and outward and filled with pale tuft clumps, by a new author_fan_clumps_field.py --part front.
previous.steps: new: author_fan_clumps_field.py (see sharedTools), step added after H33 and after the R04 rear step when that exists; the first order writes the script
previous.why: Closes gap ranks 2 and 6 (shards, thorns and leaf facets on the front; no cup or tuft from the side) and the failing R03.3, R03.4, R03.5 and R03.7. Rounds 12, 13, 15 and 16 retuned the plate-plus-flat-lens lock system four times and moved one criterion (R03.3 to partial), because a flat lens lying on a plate reads as a leaf or scale whatever its numbers; round-section clumps on their own 3D paths with no plate change the construction while keeping the outline that already passes.
previous.failureLooks: Sea urchin or porcupine (clumps radiating from one point, too thin and straight); spaghetti or a pile of sausages (even round tubes with blunt ends); dark gaps where the core shows; crinkled seams at clump roots from too small a union blend; a blob with no lock read from too much blur; the outline shrinking inside the envelope (R03.1 or R03.2 fall) or tips leaving it (figure height grows); a cup that still faces only forward, so the side view shows no pale.
previous.stallNext: Envelope plus lock relief: author the fan as one closed envelope surface from the sheet outline and depth plan, then displace it by a procedural clump relief that follows a flow field (strips that part, overlap and taper to the tips), so solidity and outline are guaranteed and only the relief is tuned.

R04.name: Ear fan rear and profile
R04.method: Layered lock sweeps from the rear, run solo: extend author_fan_lock_sweeps.py with --part rear so each rear wing lock, K crown lock and C tuft clump is its own closed swept solid (Bezier guide from r04_clumps.json re-pathed onto the spec's 3D depth plan, rounded section with a spine, convex leaf taper to a real point with tip half width at least twice the output voxel), stacked in layers with .006 to .012 tip standoff and undercut over a rear backing in place of the field core, joined to the head only in a root band buried .006 below the envelope by a wing-local fine union (voxel .0008, blend about .012 into a soft concave valley at the dome), with the outer wing swept back in plan (df .044 to .086 at u .20 to .28), the E band leaning back about .015 over its height in profile, and the C tuft tips held at least .01 below the front crown; ordered alone with the R03 front held at the baseline build, not paired.
R04.steps: new: author_fan_lock_sweeps.py --part rear replaces H34 (after H33; H35 material carry kept); the first order adds the rear part to the existing sweeps tool (shared section, taper, layer and union code with the front) and reruns the round 20 kept clump table through it as the control
R04.why: Closes the open R04.5 profile fail (straight vertical stack of leaves, no curved shell behind the cup), the R04.3 and R04.7 crease ledge and bead around the dome, and the R04.4 smooth run of leaf backs with a needle fringe, which the clump field cannot reach for the reason round 21 found on R03: unions of .003 to .006 on a .0025 voxel grid melt every groove to one or two voxels and drop tip floors below a voxel, and the strip-plus-core-plus-skin-blend leaves the ledge. It also fixes the attribution fault in the history: since round 20 (the only keep) R04 was never ordered alone, and rounds 21, 23 and 24 were all reverted on R03's verdict, so no R04 change was ever judged on R04.
R04.failureLooks: The R03 sweeps failures (pine cone or shingles, sausages, backing showing through, a root seam where the fine union meets the coarse head, whisker or ball tips) plus: a ledge or step around the dome where the root band ends; the dome swallowed or the crest at x 0 moved more than .002 (R01.4, R01.8); a picket of separate lock ends down the profile's back edge; rear locks standing in the cavity window x_side .020 to .055; crown tuft tips rising above the front fan in the front view (R03.3 regression); the swept-back wing growing the side silhouette past the crest at df .087.
R04.stallNext: Groomed hair curves to clumps for the rear wings, as for R03: Blender hair curves grown from the crown line and rear root band along the depth plan, clumped into 8 to 10 primaries per wing, converted with curve-to-mesh on a thick tapered profile and joined in the root band.
R04.respecReason: Spec section 3 (strip, core with rear face rear(u,y) - .012, skin blend, union radii .003 to .006, clump blur, and the dome valley made by I root burial into a field) describes the field construction this method replaces. The spec needs per-lock layers, tip standoff and undercut, a rear backing depth, the root-band burial and fine union with its valley width, section spine and leaf taper, and each clump path re-expressed on the depth plan (outer wing plan sweep, E band profile lean, C tuft tip ceiling below the front crown). The rear envelope table, M(u), the top dome rule, the lower edge and wing tip depth limits, the profile shell rules and the clump table rows stay.
R04.interface: blender art/species-construction/author_fan_lock_sweeps.py -- --part rear --scene <H33 head.blend> --table specs/r04_clumps.json --spec <r04-sweeps.json> --envelope <rear envelope from specs/R04.md section 3> --out <dir>. Spec: {strip (R04 section 3 S(u,y), kept), backing {depthBehindDeepest}, layers [{ids, standoff, undercut}], paths {planSweep, profileLean, tuftCeiling}, section {p, spine}, tips {profile 'leaf', minHalfWidth}, union {rootBand, burial .006, voxel, blend}, dome {protect window, blur}}. Outputs head.blend, shape.glb, fan-sweeps.json (per lock standoff and tip radius, envelope missing and extra per view, dome crest df at x 0, valley width, cavity-window intrusion, crown tuft clearance below the front crown, components, nonManifoldEdges), source-snapshot/. Invariants: one closed component, skinTopZ not above the baseline, crest within .002, no change outside the fan zone.

previous.method: The same clump volume from the rear: author_fan_clumps_field.py --part rear strips the old rear shell, plate and lock rows in field space, then grows clumps from the crown line and rear root band flowing outward and down into two tapering wings, each overlapping several neighbors, with the crown tuft as a few pointed clumps and the head dome left as a soft center.
previous.steps: new: author_fan_clumps_field.py --part rear (see sharedTools), step added after H33 and before the R03 front step
previous.why: Closes gap rank 1 (crumpled shard bowl from behind with a continuous pale lower rim and flat end planes) and R04.3, R04.4, R04.5 and R04.7. The rear lock table over a cut plate (rounds 6, 8, 9 and 11) parked after three rounds without a net gain: each pass traded combs for spools and shard tiles because the locks are decals on a displaced shell that keeps its rim and cut ends; a volume of clumps has no shell edge to make either.
previous.failureLooks: The R03 failures plus: a nest or basket weave from crossing clump paths; a hairline rim where clump ends meet the core along the lower edge; the dome swallowed into the wings (R01.4 and R01.8 regress, as in round 8); nape spikes from clumps rooted too low; a ladder or picket of clump ends down the profile's back edge.
previous.stallNext: Envelope plus lock relief for the rear wings, as for R03: a closed rear envelope from the back and side outlines displaced by flow-field clump relief that runs from the crown outward and down.

R04.review: Round 24 (parked: 3 rounds without a net gain of 1). Round 20 was the only keep, and after it R04 was never ordered alone: rounds 21, 23 and 24 were paired with R03 and all three were reverted on R03's verdict (round 21 the front clump volume read the same, round 23 the v4b closed coat read worse on R03, round 24 R03 fell 5.7 to 5), while H34, the rear clump step, ran with the same round 20 arguments in every candidate. So the method did not get a test; the three open R04 issues (profile shell fail, dome crease ledge and bead, smooth leaf-back top edge with a needle fringe) are the ones the critic listed after round 20 and are the same groove and tip faults the round 21 review traced to the field grid on the front.

R05.name: Neck and shoulders
R05.method: Authored neck column at step J: extend assemble_reconstructed_creature.py with a --neck-sections table so the bridge loft is built from sheet-derived ellipse sections (front, back, half width per world z from .424 to .497) instead of the measured stub sections, and the head and body stubs inside the fusion window are morphed radially onto that column before remeshing; in the same order add B-19r, the specified fill-only convex round of the yoke with shape_neck_shoulders_field.py (cutEnable false, back and fill off, round block, two passes), which no round has built yet.
R05.why: Round 19 showed the join parameters are exhausted: moving the cut and the fusion window removed the collar ring, but the score did not move because what keeps R05.4 failing is the column's position and shape (back .007 fit behind the sheet over the whole column in both stubs, the nape kink, the tight hourglass fillets), which the spec itself says no join parameter or body round can reach, and R05.5 and R05.6 are held by the yoke plate edge and scapular ledge, whose fill-only round (B-19r) was specified but never built. An authored column across the seam sets the neck's position and fillet radii from parameters in the one step that sees both components, and B-19r closes the yoke half.
R05.failureLooks: The head appearing to ride forward or back because the morph reached the skull or chin (check the chin front at z .48 to .50 and the fan root unchanged); a lathe-turned cylinder or bottle neck with no throat corner; a visible band where the morph window fades (z .424 or .497); a new nape bump if the back target runs behind the head's own nape; R05.1 above 1.08 or R05.2 above 1.12; from B-19r, bottle shoulders out of the hold band or ledges and nubs on the upper arms as in round 13.
R05.stallNext: Rebuild the neck as part of the head: author the head's neck stub from the same section table in a head step after H33 and the body neck top in a body step after B-23, so each component arrives at the cut already on the column and the join only bridges a .01 gap.
R05.respecReason: The spec's section 0 item 5 and friction 2 declare the .007 nape setback, the nape kink and the stem fillets out of reach and set R05.4 at partial at best; under this method they are the target. The spec must supply the authored section table (world front, back and half width per z .424 to .497, from sheet.json), the morph window and caps, the fillet radii, and the check against the chin and the fan root; its J table (offset .038, fusion window to .497) and its B-19r block stay as written.

previous.method: Assembly join parameters through loop_tools.py assemble --join at step J: lower head-trim-offset from .048 to about .02 so the head cut sits above the stub's lip at world z .465 to .477 and the bridge loft replaces it, set bridge-rings, tangent-limit and min-neck-length for a straight column, and window the fusion smoothing below z .44; then, as a separate body order, round the yoke with shape_neck_shoulders_field.py at B-19 with cutEnable false and the convex round block, no new cut.
previous.why: Closes gap rank 10 (collar ring under the fan, ledge and corner knobs from behind; R05.4, R05.5, R05.6). The ring is the head stub's depth-ramp lip, which body-only orders could never reach (round 13 left it pixel-identical); the join step now owns the seam, and the shoulder outline already matches within about .01 of figure height, so the yoke needs fill-only rounding rather than another cut.
previous.failureLooks: A neck that grows taller or shorter so the head rides up (check figure height and R05.1); a trumpet flare or a thin stem at the bridge from over-smoothing; a new horizontal seam where the loft meets the head; bottle shoulders or dropped caps from rounding too far; upper-arm ledges and corner nubs as in round 13.
previous.stallNext: A neck-and-yoke generator run on the joined skin after assembly: an analytic column and trapezius loft from the R05 section tables morphed in over the seam window, so the neck is authored once across both components.

R05.interface: assemble_reconstructed_creature.py gains --neck-sections <json> (passed through loop_tools assemble --join as neck-sections): {"rows": [{"z", "front", "back", "halfWidth", "exp"}] in world units, "morph": {"zBelow", "zAbove", "fade", "maxShift"}, "fillet": {"jawRadius", "baseRadius"}}. Without the flag the assembler behaves exactly as now. With it: (1) the loft rings are superellipses from the table, interpolated in z; (2) every stub vertex inside the window moves along its horizontal ray from the column axis to the authored section at its z, weighted by a smooth z and angle falloff, capped at maxShift; (3) the jaw-to-neck and neck-to-trapezius fillets are blended at the given radii; then the existing remesh and fusion smoothing run. The record adds neckSections with target and achieved front, back and half width per row. The builder writes the table from sheet.json through the spec frame (world y = 1.8605 x - .011), the back edge running .0133 fit at the nape to .0188 at y .26.

review.parkReason: 3 rounds without a net gain of 1
review.diagnosis: The J half of the method worked as far as it can (ring gone, R05.1 1.070, R05.2 1.083) and reached the limit the spec predicted; the remaining neck faults are position and shape of the stubs, not the seam. The yoke half was never ordered, so the shoulder criteria could not move.

R06.name: Torso and pelvis
R06.method: Joint trunk and arm-root order judged in the posed frame: the B-20T author_trunk_sections_field.py loft set to the sheet waist (back edge -.014 at .44, waist depth about .085, the round 21 v01 or v08 table) together with the B-23 rebuild_arms_field.py fillet lowered (fillet.low about .03, lowZ about .25) so the armpit flare stops making the front hourglass, accepted on posed/shaded-left and posed/shaded-front (hands on hips, tail free) with the rubric repoints H1, H2 and H4 from specs/R06.md landed first.
steps: B-23 (fillet block only; R07 keeps the paw, claw and deltoid parameters)

rubric prerequisite: R06.6 and R06.7 read the model side from render/torso.json mesh sections (H1); R06.2 compares with the sheet's leftmost run over .40 to .48 (.0816) or is retired (H2); R06.9 adds posed/shaded-left.png and R06.3 and R06.5 add posed/shaded-front.png (H4)
R06.why: The loft already moves the trunk where the sheet is (round 21: v01 and v08 newly pass R06.12, R06.13 and R06.14) but every candidate read 'same' because the critic judges m02 left, where the hanging arm covers the lumbar hollow (picture change .007 to .02), and because R06.2 and R06.6 measure the sheet's depth at .40 and the arm, so no trunk can pass them together with R06.12 (specs/R06.md H1, H2). Moving acceptance to the posed frame, retiring the contradiction and handing the front pinch to the arm-root fillet that sets it (H5) lets the measured gains reach the score and closes gap rank 4 and the R06 half of rank 8.
R06.failureLooks: The posed side still reads as a plank because the akimbo forearm now hides the waist at .47 to .49 (check the white gap under the arm at .385 to .46); a crater or shelf at the armpit when the lower fillet leaves the trunk loft's held half widths at .36 to .38 uncovered; R07.6 posed arm IoU dropping as the fillet changes the arm root; a wasp waist if the back edge goes past -.014; R06.1 front waist over 1.10 if the half widths are raised to soften the hourglass.
R06.stallNext: If the posed-frame critic still reads a plank with the sheet waist built, the gap is the dorsal S and rump the tails hide: build the rump and lumbar sway from the tail-free root (body-0086/attempt-03) with rebuild_body_field.py driven by a trunk spline, rerun the downstream body steps, and judge with tails hidden.

review.stalled: Rounds 15, 20 and 21 moved the trunk measurably the right way (round 21 v01: R06.12 1.163 to 1.064, R06.13 .885 to .968, R06.14 .836 to .992) but the critic read 'same' every time, because its image m02 left shows the hanging arm over the waist and R06.2 and R06.6 measure the sheet's .40 depth and the arm, so the best trunk loses as many measured passes as it gains. The spec named these as H1, H2 and H4 on 2026-10-01; they were never landed, so retuning the station table could not register.

previous.method: Author the trunk from parameters: a new author_trunk_sections_field.py lofts superellipse sections from a station table read from sheet.json (side front and back edges and front half widths every .02 of figure height from y .26 to .62) and weighted-morphs the native trunk toward that field inside a trunk mask that excludes the arms, the neck above .26, the thighs below the hip freeze and the held tail root.
previous.steps: new: art/species-construction/author_trunk_sections_field.py, runner blender, args --body <shape.glb> --fairing <fairing.json> --spec <trunk-sections.json> --out <dir>; spec: stations [{y, front, back, halfWidth, expFront, expBack}], mask {armRadius from fairing armJoints, neckTop, hipFreeze, tailRootZone from species.json zones}, morph fade (at least ten times the relief change); outputs body.blend, shape.glb, fairing.json with a trunkSections record (per station target and achieved front, back and half width), source-snapshot/. Step inserted after B-20 and before B-21, so the arm rebuild B-23 fillets onto the new trunk.
previous.why: Closes gap rank 5 (plank profile: side chest depth .131 against .168, waist 1.30x, chest over waist 1.07 against 1.54; R06.6, R06.7, R06.9) and rank 15 (rump depth). reshape_torso_field.py parked after three rounds because it maps the measured edges of the previous mesh, so every depth change also carried its belts and ledges into new bands or thinned the waist (rounds 3, 9, 15); a lofted section stack sets depth and cross section directly and a weighted morph leaves no ring (LESSONS, field-space corrections).
previous.failureLooks: A lathe-turned vase or tube with too-regular sections; belt lines at the morph mask edges; a crater or shelf at the armpit, deltoid or thigh root where the mask ends; a dent at the tail root (R10 and R11 are held and must not move); a pigeon breast that breaks R06.8; hips widening off the posed front band (R06.10).
previous.stallNext: Generate the trunk on the tail-free root (body-0086/attempt-03) with rebuild_body_field.py driven by a trunk spline and section radii, then rerun the downstream body steps, so the trunk is built rather than morphed.

R07.name: Arms and forepaws
R07.method: Digit-chain forepaw built in field space inside rebuild_arms_field.py at B-23 (new paw mode 'digits'): a domed palm pad plus four two-segment digit capsule chains, each with its own root, lateral fan yaw, palmward pitch, tapering radii and curl, ending in a claw sheath that follows the last segment, all in a paw frame rolled by pawRollDeg about the wrist axis, unioned with the arm rod by smin at the wrist; the arm rod keeps round 22's thinner forearm and wrist and the ARM-dict deltoid.
steps: new (first order builds it): rebuild_arms_field.py gains ARM['paw'] = {'mode': 'lobes' (default, every earlier run exact) | 'digits', 'rollDeg': 15 to 25 (applied to the paw frame and faded into the rod over wrist +-.02), 'palm': {'s', 'radii': [ru, rv, rs], 'domeOffset', 'blend'}, 'digits': list of 4 {'rootS', 'rootR', 'yawDeg' (lateral fan, outer digits outward), 'pitchDeg', 'segLen': [2], 'radii': [root, joint, tip] as (width, thickness), 'curlDeg': [2]}, 'digitBlend', 'grooveBlend', 'claw': {'length', 'baseRadius', 'bend', 'inset'} with optional per-digit overrides}; it writes paw joints (palm center, each digit root, joint, tip and claw tip) into fairing.json armJoints and the achieved paw over wrist width, tip arch over knuckle width, front-view claw-tip spread and claw visible length into arm-field.json. Inputs and outputs otherwise unchanged (--body, --fairing, --spec, --out).
R07.why: The lobe paw stalled on its representation, not its numbers: lobes are parallel capsules on fixed lateral offsets with one width radius root to tip and the paw frame is unrolled, so the spec's own structural keys (lobeTipWidthRadius, pawRollDeg) do not exist in the tool and round 22 could only shrink and sharpen the mitten, giving paw over wrist 1.2 instead of 1.5, a closed human fist in profile (R07.4 pass to partial) and the same single claw column in front (R07.5); round 11's pits and round 16's needle claws came from the same capsule saddle and edge-on frame. Separate fanned, tapered digit chains with their own claw sheaths in a rolled frame build the arch, the tip spread and the curved claw directly (R07.3, R07.4, R07.5, audit rank 7), while keeping round 22's slimmer forearm, which all three readers preferred, and the authored deltoid (R07.1). R07.6 is not closed by any arm: the spec measures the sheet's front and back disagreeing on the right side by .028 (best reachable mean .867 to .871), so it needs the spec's proposed per-view registration or a .87 floor from the orchestrator.
R07.failureLooks: A human hand or starfish (free digits past .03 fit, visible gaps between digits, splay wider than the knuckles); pits or creases where digit chains meet the palm; a lumpy bead chain at the digit joints; claws stuck to the dorsum instead of leaving the tips; a twist band across the wrist from the roll; the posed front paw outside the hip outline; R07.6 below .862.
R07.stallNext: Sculpt the forepaw as one closed implicit from a sheet-traced dorsum and edge outline pair (two orthographic profile curves intersected and rounded, as the hind-paw profile-curve instep), with claws added as local cones; if that also stalls, park R07 for Nick with the R07.6 frame question.
R07.respecReason: The spec's counted structure (paw body, four digit lobes, four claws, deltoid, thin forearm and wrist, roll of 15 to 25 degrees, tip arch .80 to .85 of the knuckles) is what the digit chains build; only the tool keys change, which is not a reason to rewrite it.
R07.previous: Analytic arm and forepaw rebuild with rebuild_arms_field.py at step B-23, enlarging the paw to about 1.5 wrist widths with four separately grooved digit lobes and claws leaving each tip at about a third of the digit length, and authoring the deltoid cap from the ARM dict instead of keeping the native shoulder.

review.reason: parked: 3 rounds without a net gain of 1
review.whyStalled: The lobe generator cannot express the spec's arch, roll or tip taper (no such keys), so the planner shrank the mitten with existing keys and got a closed fist with one claw column.

R08.name: Legs
R08.method: Station-table resample with reshape_legs_field.py at step B-22 (yMask and zBlur kept) for the remaining sculpt: one calf swell into a slim Achilles line, a soft kneecap plane, the ankle-top crease removed, and the outer thigh and lateral shin lines moved out to the posed bands.
R08.why: Closes gap rank 12 (double calf swell and knee knob; R08.10 thigh band .830, R08.11 shin band .643) now that the widths pass; these are outline and surface adjustments on correct structure, which a resample does. Rank 16 (rest stance .44 against .31) is a joint position the posed fit already corrects and stays a refinement.
R08.failureLooks: Horizontal ripple bands or a crease at the morph edges (ankle top, thigh root); a tail dent from the depth pass if the yMask slips; the calf back line thinning off the posed shin band (round 14); a bowed shin path.
R08.stallNext: Loft the lower leg along the knee-to-ankle axis from the R08 section table (the spec's own recommended construction) in a new lower-leg generator, morphed in between y .74 and .925.

R09.name: Hind paws
R09.method: Analytic hind-paw rebuild with rebuild_hind_paws_field.py at step B-21, replacing the straight dorsum capsule with a profile-curve instep (a convex dome rising from the claw roots to the ankle) and a heel rounded into the sole, with graded toe lobes and claws rooted inside the toe tips.
R09.newOptions: a PAW key for the side top-line curve (control points from the claw roots to the ankle front) with a default that keeps earlier runs exact
R09.why: Closes gap rank 11 (slipper with a vertical heel cliff and no instep; beads in a row; claws on the toe faces; R09.9 foot band .647, R09.3, R09.8). The paw is already authored from parameters; the ellipsoid table's straight dorsum slope is what builds the ramp, and a curve-driven top line closes what the table cannot.
R09.failureLooks: A clog or club foot (instep too high, toes buried); a heel bulb or ankle step at the morph band; pits between toes; pearl-headed claws; the sole lifting off the floor contact.
R09.stallNext: Rebuild the paw as a lofted section stack along the paw axis from a side profile curve and a front arch curve, with the toes as separate lobes unioned on top.
R09.respecReason: The spec's mass 7 makes the dorsum one straight capsule slope from the ankle front to the toe bases and builds the instep as a separate ellipsoid, which is the ramp the audit names; the new top line is a convex arc with its crest about a third of the paw length back.

R12.name: Whole-form coherence
R12.method: Coat masses from the fan's clump primitive: a new body step author_coat_masses_field.py after B-23 reuses the clump sweep module of author_fan_clumps_field.py to add broad, low, soft coat masses at the sternum, forearms and calves, with one shared set of section and taper settings for the fan, the face tufts and the body, so the whole figure reads as one fur.
R12.steps: new: art/species-construction/author_coat_masses_field.py, runner blender, args --body <shape.glb> --fairing <fairing.json> --spec <coat-masses.json> --out <dir>; spec: masses [{id, region zone, root, path, section, relief at most .004 of figure height}] plus the shared idiom file; outputs body.blend, shape.glb, fairing.json with a coatMasses record; written only after the fan clump module exists
R12.why: Closes gap rank 4 (a hard jagged fan on a bare vinyl body; R12.1, R12.2). It depends on the fan clumps existing and passing, so R12 stays parked until R03 and R04 land on the clump method and the parts reach 5, as its park reason says.
R12.failureLooks: Fur collars or ruffs the R05 spec forbids; locks on the legs against R08's surface rule; lumps that break measured outlines; a body coat in a different idiom (scales, leaves) from the fan.
R12.stallNext: Unify the idiom on the fan and face tufts only and leave body coat masses to the later surface pass.

friction: R06: the spec's side depth table (peak .129 at .34 to .36) and the gap audit's sheet reading (.168 at .36) disagree by about 30 percent; the respec must re-measure from sheet.json before any number is used.

R07: the spec's 'oversized paw' cap (dorsum at most .046) contradicts the audit's measured sheet paw (.055 in the posed front, 1.5 wrist widths); the audit read the paw on the hip in the posed view, the spec in the arms-down view, so the respec should state which view each number belongs to.

R12 against R05 and R08: the audit asks for chest, forearm and calf coat masses, while the R05 spec forbids any ruff and the R08 spec forbids fur locks or tufts on the leg. The coat masses planned for R12 are broad low relief, not locks, but the specs need one shared rule before R12 unparks.
